project.name: code2req
project.vision: Spec-Driven Development (SDD) — treating a highly structured, technology-agnostic business specification as the primary, authoritative artifact from which automated tests, clean implementation, and functional documentation are derived.
project.elevator_pitch: An AI-driven CLI that reverse-engineers legacy enterprise codebases into structured business specifications organized by functional flows, with full traceability back to source code.
project.problem_statement: Legacy enterprise codebases contain embedded business rules, domain validations, and ecosystem invariants that are obscured by technical debt and scattered across REST endpoints, async event handlers, and hidden procedural database layers — making systems hard to understand, test, and re-architect.
goals: De-technify enterprise code — abstract dense, legacy implementations into clear business intentions, process parameters, and edge cases
Eradicate context rot & hallucinations — enforce stateless, short-lived execution with absolute context isolation per file
Provide end-to-end visibility — connect scattered functional points across frontend, REST, async events, and database layers
Provide a standard data contract for test generation — output predictable structured semantic graphs bridging static code and dynamic business tests

stakeholders.name: Developer
concerns: Quickly understand legacy codebases without manual reading
Extract business rules obscured by technical debt
Generate structured specifications from source code

stakeholders.name: Tech Lead
concerns: No leakage of secrets or credentials
Confidence that extracted specifications are accurate

user_personas.name: Developer
goals: Understand what business rules a legacy codebase implements
Generate structured specifications without manual effort
Identify all endpoints, event handlers, and database interactions
pain_points: Spending hours reading through dense legacy code
Missing hidden business rules in stored procedures or custom validators
Lack of documentation on system behavior and edge cases
user_personas.context: Works with Java/Spring codebases daily. Needs to quickly onboard to unfamiliar legacy systems or document existing ones for compliance and refactoring.

user_personas.name: Tech Lead
goals: Ensure sensitive data never leaves local machine
pain_points: No reliable way to get a bird's-eye view of a legacy system
Risk of hardcoded secrets leaking through AI pipelines
Difficulty tracing async event flows across services
user_personas.context: Responsible for architectural decisions and compliance. Needs to trust the tool's output and verify nothing sensitive is exposed.

in_scope: YAML manifest parsing for multi-repository scan configuration
Optional Maven dependency graph resolution with graceful fallback
Java source file AST parsing using JavaParser (component types, HTTP endpoints, event listeners, scheduled task/trigger detection, method calls, custom validators)
In-memory secret redaction (passwords, API keys, credentials) before any LLM processing
Exclude pattern filtering for generated code and vendor packages
Structured JSON index output (code-graph-index.json) with full structural metadata
SQLite task store ingestion via Spring JDBC with WAL mode and idempotent task IDs
Global declaration registry for inter-file method resolution (Pass 1)
Inter-file call graph resolution via CallGraphVisitor (Pass 2)
Outbound HTTP client detection and floating link resolution (RestTemplate, WebClient, @FeignClient, FloatingLinkResolver)
Deterministic topic link resolution (producer-to-consumer matching across Kafka, RabbitMQ, ActiveMQ)
Extended SQLite tables (execution_findings, topic_links, floating_links, metrics)
CLI scan command — Phase 1 deterministic two-pass execution
out_of_scope: Phase 2 — Stateful Dynamic Execution (LLM-powered analysis per file)
Phase 3 — Cascaded Semantic Synthesis (map-reduce, Markdown/JSON output)
Frontend or UI code analysis (JavaScript, TypeScript, HTML)
Code modification or mutation on disk (read-only operation)

technical: Pure Java — no native OS bindings or JNI (no Tree-sitter)
JavaParser for AST analysis — mandatory, not optional
SQLite as embedded persistence — no external database
No network required during Phase 1 indexing
compliance: Read-only operation — zero modifications to source files
Zero secret leakage — hardcoded credentials must be redacted before any outbound call

success_metrics.measurement: Verification matching entry paths found in the static code graph against expected endpoints in target codebase
Fields annotated with custom validators have corresponding isValid logic slices extracted
Methods annotated with @Scheduled have their cron/fixed-delay/fixed-rate expressions captured and linked to the business operations they initiate
Processing tasks that reach SUCCESS state (excluding AWAITING_HUMAN_REVIEW)
Zero exceptions due to file locks when executing under pool-size of 10 with WAL mode

success_metrics.target: 0 tokens consumed on re-scan of unchanged workspace
success_metrics.measurement: Re-running against unmodified workspace completes using 100% cached records in <= 60 seconds
Time to resolve pending/orphaned states and re-align the processing DAG after crash
Ratio of resolved MethodCallExpr nodes to total non-JDK MethodCallExpr nodes in the codebase
Verification that all @Procedure annotations and JdbcTemplate calls are captured
Verification that all RestTemplate/WebClient/FeignClient usages are registered as floating_links
Cross-reference of matching topic/queue/destination pairs between producers and consumers

non_functional_requirements.description: Phase 1 indexing must complete without network calls or LLM interactions
non_functional_requirements.acceptance_criteria: Zero outbound HTTP calls during scan command execution

non_functional_requirements.description: Hardcoded secrets must be redacted in-memory before any LLM processing
non_functional_requirements.acceptance_criteria: Passwords, API keys, and credentials replaced with [REDACTED:type] placeholders; original file on disk untouched

non_functional_requirements.description: Graceful degradation when optional dependency resolution fails
non_functional_requirements.acceptance_criteria: Tool proceeds with standalone heuristic mode when Maven is absent or project does not compile; clear warning logged

non_functional_requirements.description: Idempotent task identification to prevent redundant processing
non_functional_requirements.acceptance_criteria: Task IDs computed from SHA-256 of file path, content hash, test content hash, model ID, and prompt version

non_functional_requirements.description: WAL mode enabled in SQLite for concurrent read/write
non_functional_requirements.acceptance_criteria: PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL and busy_timeout=5000 set on connection initialization

risks.description: JavaParser fails on complex or vendor-specific syntax constructs
risks.mitigation: Annotation-driven fallback strategy — classify components by annotation presence even when type resolution fails

risks.description: Maven depgraph plugin unavailable or incompatible with target project
risks.mitigation: Graceful failure with clear warning; standalone heuristic mode proceeds without dependency metadata

risks.description: SQLite locking under concurrent access during Phase 2 (design concern carried forward)
risks.mitigation: WAL mode + busy_timeout + connection pool configured upfront in Phase 1 implementation

risks.description: Process crash during Phase 1 leaves SQLite task store in inconsistent state with orphaned RUNNING tasks
risks.mitigation: Startup orphan detection and reconciliation; resume command for explicit warm-start recovery

risks.description: Secret redaction misses non-standard credential patterns or produces false positives on benign values
risks.mitigation: Pattern-based detection with documented coverage scope; in-memory only operation limits blast radius

risks.description: JavaParser version incompatibility with Java language features used in target codebase (e.g., records, sealed classes, pattern matching)
risks.mitigation: Pin compatible JavaParser version; graceful parse failure per file with logged error does not block full scan

assumptions: Maven is the build system (pom.xml) — Gradle support is future scope
User has JDK 21+ installed for running the tool
LLM provider credentials are configured separately (not part of Phase 1)

definition_of_done: Code compiles and builds without errors
Feature matches the acceptance criteria defined in the user story
CLI scan command produces valid code-graph-index.json for the petclinic target
definition_of_ready: Story has clearly defined acceptance criteria
Dependencies on other stories are identified
Story is small enough to complete in a single work session

epics.name: Deterministic Multi-Language Indexing
epics.description: Before any LLM interaction, the CLI scans the physical workspace using pure-Java AST parsers (JavaParser) to map signatures, endpoint routes, call frameworks, and event publishers. Produces a local intermediate JSON contract and populates the SQLite task store. Runs as a deterministic compiler-pass requiring zero network connectivity or LLM credentials.

epics.name: Language Extension Framework
epics.description: Define a common parser abstraction (SPI) so that adding support for new programming languages does not require modifying the core pipeline. Language parsers implement a shared contract and are discovered at runtime. The rest of the pipeline (redaction, output, orchestration) remains parser-agnostic.

features.name: Project Configuration & Manifest Parsing
features.description: Parse project-manifest.yaml, resolve scan targets against the filesystem, validate configuration structure and required fields.
features.background: A valid project-manifest.yaml file exists in the current working directory with at least one scan target defined.
business_rules: All scan target paths must be accessible on the local filesystem — the CLI validates existence before processing
The manifest schema must conform to the expected YAML structure; unrecognized fields produce warnings but don't block execution
If a scan target directory lacks Java source files, the CLI logs a warning and skips it rather than failing

user_stories.title: Developer defines scan targets in project manifest
Developer recovers gracefully from manifest errors

features.name: Dependency Graph Resolution
features.description: Optional Maven dependency resolution with graceful fallback to standalone heuristic mode when Maven is unavailable.
features.background: Manifest parsed and scan targets resolved.
business_rules: If Maven is unavailable or pom.xml is missing, CLI proceeds with standalone heuristic mode and logs a clear warning
Dependency resolution is optional — the pipeline never blocks or fails on Maven failure

features.name: Java Source AST Analysis (JavaParser implementation)
features.description: JavaParser-based scanning for Java/Spring codebases: component types, HTTP endpoints, event listeners, method calls, custom validators, scheduled tasks, and message broker event flows (Kafka, RabbitMQ, ActiveMQ/JMS). This is the reference implementation of the LanguageParser SPI.
features.background: Scan target directories resolved and accessible.
business_rules: JavaParser processes each file independently — a single parse failure does not stop the full scan
Component classification uses annotation presence as the primary heuristic, with structural fallback when type resolution fails
Only .java files under scan targets are processed; other types are silently ignored

features.name: Secret Redaction & Exclude Filtering
features.description: In-memory redaction of passwords/keys/credentials before any LLM processing + exclude pattern filtering for generated/vendor code.
features.background: Source files parsed and content prepared for output.
business_rules: Redaction operates in-memory only — source files on disk are never touched
Redacted values use [REDACTED:type] placeholders (e.g. [REDACTED:password])
Exclude patterns follow .gitignore-style glob matching against file paths
Generated code and vendor packages are excluded by default

user_stories.title: Developer filters out generated and vendor code

features.name: Index Output & SQLite Persistence
features.description: Generate code-graph-index.json + SQLite task store with WAL mode and idempotent task IDs.
features.background: AST analysis and redaction completed for all targets.
business_rules: SQLite uses WAL journal mode + 5000ms busy timeout
Task IDs are deterministic SHA-256 hashes — never random
If the output directory is unwritable, CLI fails with a clear message rather than partial output

features.name: CLI Scan Orchestration
features.description: Phase 1 scan command that orchestrates the full pipeline end-to-end.
business_rules: The scan command must never make network calls or LLM interactions (Phase 1 only)
Progress reported per stage (manifest → deps → AST → redact → persist) with timing and file counts
Stage failure reports which stage failed and exits non-zero

user_stories.title: Developer runs a full Phase 1 scan

features.name: Parser Abstraction SPI
features.description: Define a LanguageParser interface with a common output contract (components, endpoints, events, validators, tasks). Each language provides its own implementation. Contracts use optional fields so parsers can support a subset of capabilities.
features.background: The core pipeline has been implemented and is ready to accept parser-agnostic input.
business_rules: The SPI must define a single LanguageParser interface that all language parsers implement
The output contract must use optional fields — a parser can support only components without implementing endpoints or validators
The contract must be technology-agnostic (no Java/Spring-specific types in the interface)

user_stories.title: Developer defines a common parser contract
Developer implements a new language parser

features.name: Parser Discovery & Routing
features.description: A registry that maps file extensions to parsers. Discovers available parsers at startup and routes each source file to the correct parser based on its extension.
features.background: The LanguageParser SPI is defined and at least one parser implementation exists.
business_rules: Parser registration maps one or more file extensions to a single parser
If no parser is registered for a file extension, the file is logged as unsupported and skipped — it does not block the scan
If multiple parsers claim the same extension, the first registered wins with a warning logged

user_stories.title: Developer registers a new parser for a language
CLI routes files to the correct parser by extension

features.name: Shared Pipeline Integration
features.description: Wire the parser SPI into the existing pipeline (US013-US016) so that redaction, exclude filtering, output generation, and orchestration work with any parser's output without modification.
features.background: Parser SPI, discovery, and at least one parser implementation exist.
business_rules: Adding a new language parser must not require changes to the core pipeline (redaction, output, orchestration)
The shared output schema must accommodate language-specific metadata in optional fields

user_stories.title: Developer adds a parser without changing the pipeline

features.name: Two-Pass Pipeline Orchestration & Call Graph Resolution
features.description: Two-pass deterministic linker: Pass 1 collects method signatures into a GlobalDeclarationRegistry; Pass 2 resolves MethodCallExpr nodes against the registry to produce CallGraphEdge records. Overloaded methods recorded as AMBIGUOUS when arguments cannot discriminate.
features.background: Phase 4a (ComponentVisitor, EndpointVisitor) completed. Pipeline refactored to two-pass orchestration.
business_rules: Pass 1 extracts method signatures, field types, and component stereotypes — no resolution or analysis is performed
Pass 2 resolves each MethodCallExpr against the declaration registry built in Pass 1
Calls matching internal package boundaries are recorded with source file, target file, and method signatures
Overloaded methods are recorded as AMBIGUOUS when argument count cannot discriminate
Calls to JDK, Spring internals, and unresolvable third-party libraries are recorded as unresolved_signatures
Post-pass runs TopicLinkResolver and FloatingLinkResolver after all files are processed
Parse errors in one file do not block processing of other files

user_stories.title: Developer upgrades pipeline to two-pass orchestration

features.name: Database Access Detection
features.description: Detect database access patterns via DbAccessVisitor: JdbcTemplate, @Procedure, EntityManager, @Transactional, NamedParameterJdbcTemplate, SimpleJdbcCall. Spring Data interfaces registered as virtual declarations.
features.background: Two-pass pipeline operational. Pass 1 registry available.
business_rules: Detect JdbcTemplate.update/query/queryForObject calls with SQL extraction
Detect @Procedure(name) on repository methods
Detect EntityManager.persist/merge/find/createQuery
Detect @Transactional on method or class level as transaction boundaries
Spring Data interfaces (CrudRepository, JpaRepository) registered as virtual database access points

features.name: Outbound HTTP Detection & Floating Link Resolution
features.description: Detect outbound HTTP calls via RestClientVisitor (RestTemplate, WebClient, @FeignClient). Post-pass FloatingLinkResolver matches HTTP calls to known endpoints deterministically.
features.background: Two-pass pipeline operational. Pass 1 registry available.
business_rules: Detect RestTemplate.getForObject/postForObject/exchange with URL extraction
Detect WebClient fluent builder chains (method/uri/retrieve)
Detect @FeignClient(name, url) on interfaces
URL literals captured as-is; SpEL/environment expressions captured as patterns with isExpression flag
FloatingLinkResolver matches URL patterns to known endpoints: literal match = RESOLVED 1.0, path variable match = RESOLVED 0.8

features.name: Topic Link Resolution
features.description: Deterministic post-pass resolver matching event producers to consumers across Kafka, RabbitMQ, and ActiveMQ/JMS. Matches on broker + topic_or_queue values.
features.background: Kafka, RabbitMQ, and ActiveMQ visitors complete (Phase 4d, 4g, 4h). All event flows captured.
business_rules: Matches broker + topic_or_queue between producers and consumers
Each matching pair creates a topic_link row with status RESOLVED
Covers Kafka, RabbitMQ, and ActiveMQ/JMS within the same manifest execution

user_stories.title: Developer links event producers to consumers

features.name: Extended SQLite Tables & Metrics
features.description: Extended SQLite schema for structured trace persistence: execution_findings, topic_links, floating_links, and metrics tables alongside the existing tasks table.
features.background: All resolution and link visitors complete.
business_rules: execution_findings table stores per-task structured findings with schema_version
topic_links table stores deterministic producer-consumer matches
floating_links table stores outbound HTTP calls with resolution status
metrics table stores run-level counters (edges, links, tokens consumed)
